findings.title: Match count overwritten instead of accumulated in SIMD regexp path
findings.message: In `RegExpMatchGlobalAtom_OneCharPattern`, the SIMD-optimized implementation stores its match count with an assignment `*number_of_matches = matches` rather than accumulation `*number_of_matches += matches`. The caller (`RegExpMatchGlobalAtom`) first calls `RegExpResultsCache_MatchGlobalAtom::TryGet` which, on a cache hit, pre-populates `number_of_matches` with the previously cached count before invoking the dispatch function. The assignment inside the SIMD path silently discards this cached count and replaces it with only the new (incremental) count. The corrupted value (which can be 0 when no additional matches exist beyond the cached position) is then stored back into the cache via `TryInsert`. On the next call with the same subject/pattern, `TryGet` retrieves the corrupted cache entry with `number_of_matches == 0`, immediately triggering the `DCHECK_GT(number_of_matches, 0)` assertion in the caller.
findings.suggestion: Change the assignment to accumulation so that matches found in a prior (cached) invocation are preserved. The caller passes in the already-populated `number_of_matches` from a cache hit and expects the SIMD path to add onto it, not replace it.

ground_truth.root_cause: The original scalar loop incremented `*number_of_matches` in-place (`(*number_of_matches)++`), naturally accumulating across any prior cached value. The SIMD rewrite introduced a local `int matches = 0` accumulator for vectorized counting efficiency, but the final store was written as assignment (`*number_of_matches = matches`) rather than as accumulation (`*number_of_matches += matches`), breaking the API contract that the output pointer is an in-out parameter when called after a cache hit.
